subject: Subprocessor delta: coordination window and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morgan <kate.morgan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor delta: coordination window and rollback criteria

Hi Kate —

Quick note following our intake form: we have a small subprocessor change planned that will affect telemetry routing for a subset of EU customers but also touches a US telemetry relay used by Acme for debug logs. We want to schedule the change to minimize impact and provide the evidence you asked for.

High level:
- Change: swap runtime-relay-v3 -> runtime-relay-v4 (new vendor: StreamBridge Ltd.)
- Scope: telemetry-only (observability traces and debug logs); not customer PII or model prompt content
- Proposed maintenance window: 2026-09-16 01:00–03:00 UTC (low traffic)

Attached: subprocessor_delta_manifest_v2.xlsx (contains the roster diff and data-path diagrams) and evidence_summary_0909.pdf (high-level attestations).

Requests for Acme:
1) Please confirm if the proposed window works for your SRE/ops team.
2) Any additional evidence or exportability information you require for procurement/legal before we proceed?

We can also include rollback conditions and a canary monitor. Proposed rollback criteria (preliminary):
- Any increase in error rate >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes on production paths used by Acme
- Latency p95 degradation >200ms above baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows
- Any loss of message delivery to your ingestion endpoint for >60s

If these look reasonable we will finalize the cutover playbook and share a runbook with contact lines and PagerDuty incident links.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

----
From: Kate Morgan <kate.morgan@acmecorp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCorp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor delta: coordination window and rollback criteria

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the heads-up and the attachments. A few quick questions before we lock a window: 

1) Can you confirm whether any logs will be replicated to StreamBridge’s storage buckets in the EU? Our data residency policy requires proof that storage stays within the same jurisdiction.
2) The manifest spreadsheet shows a temporary service account with cross-account access — can we see the IAM bindings and the access expiration on that account?
3) Who is the StreamBridge security contact for audit requests (SOC report or equivalent)?

Our procurement/legal team will want the exportability note and an explicit statement that no customer account tokens or prompt content are being routed to the new processor. If you can provide the IAM snapshot and an on-call contact by EOD tomorrow (09/10), we can confirm the maintenance window.

—Kate
Kate Morgan
Head of Security Programs
AcmeCorp

----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morgan <kate.morgan@acmecorp.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor delta: coordination window and rollback criteria

Hi Kate — looping in Marissa from Platform so we can answer the IAM/replication questions. Quick responses inline: 

1) Storage: StreamBridge will not persist customer observability payloads outside of their EU regional cluster for EU-origin traffic. For US-origin debug logs (the path Acme uses for some debug streams) we will route to a US-only bucket owned by StreamBridge’s US entity; however we will provide exportability controls and a TTL of 14 days by default. We will put the relevant bucket ARNs and geo-tags into the manifest (I attached a reference).

2) Service account: the temporary account is a short-lived role with credentials rotated hourly; binding snapshot and least-privilege policy attached in the evidence PDF. Access expiry currently set for 2026-10-01 in our staging cutover plan.

3) StreamBridge security contact: security@streambridge.com (SOC2 Type II report available; summary included in evidence_summary_0909.pdf). We will request the audit artifact and add the SOC report link to the Drive manifest.

We can provide the IAM binding export and a minimal proof-of-residency statement by EOD today.

Marissa — can you confirm the rollback automation and the canary metrics we referenced?

Thanks,
Kimberly

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Kate Morgan <kate.morgan@acmecorp.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor delta: coordination window and rollback criteria

Hi all — Marissa here. Quick operational confirmations and runbook pointers: 

- Canary: we will shift 3% of Acme’s telemetry to runtime-relay-v4 for the first 15 minutes, monitor delivery success and latency. If canary metrics are green (no rule tripped), we increment to 25% for 30 minutes, then to 100% after a final health window.
- Rollback automation: runbook will automatically remove StreamBridge from the route if any rollback criterion is met. Engineers will also perform a manual rollback if a critical alert fires.
- PagerDuty: incident link created for the change (see related_links). On-call rotation: Platform SRE primary is +1 (pagerduty id PR-54321); backup is +2.
- Artifacts we will add to Drive today: IAM binding export (.json), bucket ARNs and geo-tags (.xlsx), and StreamBridge SOC2 summary (.pdf).

Kate — we’ll attach the IAM snapshot and the residency statement to the Drive link and send a follow-up email when complete. If Acme signs off by EOD 09/10 we’ll start the pre-cutover rehearsals next week.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Product Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

----
